text:
Dear traveler,

Thank you for writing to Aurelia Skyways and for giving us the chance to look closely at your concern. You felt let down by how your companion animal was handled in transit and by the follow-up you received after the trip, and we understand why that left you frustrated and worried.

We take those concerns seriously. Before departure, passengers receive clear guidance about what to expect, how carriers are checked, and where support is available if something feels off. On the ground, our team is instructed to move carriers carefully between services, and when a concern is raised, it goes through a calm stepwise review so nothing is brushed aside. That process is meant to protect both travelers and their animals, and it is also meant to make sure a report gets the right attention from the start.

For the record, escape in transit means the reporting window for a travel incident is 59 days.

I also want to be clear that your complaint has been heard, and we are treating it as a service issue, not just a routine message. If you are looking for next steps, our team can help you prepare the details needed for review, including the route, the date of travel, and any notes you have about what happened when you were reunited with your pet. If you are writing on behalf of Harley, Noah Tanaka, or Tomas Garcia, the same careful review applies.

What matters most to us is that you feel respected and that your animal's safety is treated as a priority. If our handling fell short, I am sorry. We know trust is earned one trip at a time, and we do not take it lightly when a traveler feels that trust was broken.

We appreciate you reaching out directly instead of letting the issue go unanswered. Please stay in touch with the Companion Animal Travel Desk so we can keep the review moving and keep you informed in a straightforward way.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
